title: Mass Spec in Practice: Drug Confirmation, 2-HG and Ambient MS in Surgery
summary: Learn why a drug immunoassay is only a presumptive screen confirmed by mass spectrometry, how mutant IDH produces the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate, and how ambient mass spectrometry devices (DESI, MasSpec Pen, iKnife, Mini 12) bring tissue answers toward the operating room.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 5 Hits 1, 10 and 11 and Trap 6. Checked against Reschly-Krasowski 2018, Argoff 2018, Chou 2021, Phelps 2018, Van Hese 2022 and Garza 2024 (Europe PMC full text), Santagata 2014, Zhang 2017 and Li 2014 (read via a page-fetch tool), and the Balog 2013 abstract. The reviewer’s “immunoassays err toward false positives” is qualified: the sources also report false negatives (drugs poorly detected by the screen), and definitive MS testing can be used first, not only to confirm (register flag rv-ch5-immunoassay-false-negatives). 2-HG is taught as an IDH-mutation marker in glioma and in other IDH-mutant cancers (register flag rv-ch5-2hg-beyond-glioma). Ambient devices are taught as research or prototype tools (register flag rv-ch5-ambient-ms-research-stage). Not taught as fact: the 1981 USS Nimitz history, the “GC-MS traditionally” framing, the iKnife 1.8-second and 94.4% figures, MasSpec Pen mouse figures and Mini 12 specifications from the Number Vault (table not taught). The reviewer figure is not taught.

objectives: Explain why an immunoassay drug screen is presumptive and how mass spectrometry confirms it.
Describe how mutant IDH1/IDH2 produces 2-hydroxyglutarate and why it is called an oncometabolite.
Distinguish the DESI, MasSpec Pen, iKnife (REIMS) and Mini 12 ambient mass spectrometry approaches.

scenes.title: Three questions for the mass spectrometer
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three requests reach the mass spectrometry service. (1) A urine opiate immunoassay screen is positive in a patient taking levofloxacin who denies opioid use. (2) A neurosurgeon removing a glioma asks whether the tumour carries an IDH mutation. (3) A breast surgeon asks, during the operation, whether tissue at the margin is cancer. Question token: “Which answers can mass spectrometry give?”

cues.text: Three requests reach the mass spectrometry lab. First: a urine opiate screen is positive, but the patient takes levofloxacin and denies using opioids.
Second: a neurosurgeon removing a glioma wants to know if the tumour is IDH-mutant. Third: a breast surgeon wants to know, mid-operation, if the margin is cancer.
Which of these can mass spectrometry answer, and how?

props.label: Which answers can mass spec give?

scenes.title: Screen first, then confirm
scenes.altText: Two cards. Presumptive screen (immunoassay): inexpensive, can be run at point of care, results within minutes; antibodies target a drug or class, so cross-reacting compounds give false positives (examples from the sources: a labetalol metabolite on amphetamine immunoassays; quinolone antibiotics on some opiate immunoassays) and some drugs are poorly detected, giving false negatives (many opiate screens poorly detect oxycodone). Definitive test (mass spectrometry: GC-MS, LC-MS or LC-MS/MS): specific identification of drugs and metabolites; used to confirm positive screens or to detect drugs the immunoassay misses; it can also be used as the initial test. Token: cross-reactivity data differ between manufacturers.

cues.text: A drug screen is usually an immunoassay: cheap, fast, and possible at the point of care. But it is only presumptive.
Its antibodies can cross-react. A labetalol metabolite can trigger an amphetamine screen, and quinolone antibiotics can trigger some opiate screens: false positives.
It can also miss drugs. Many opiate screens detect oxycodone poorly, so a negative screen does not rule a drug out.
Mass spectrometry, by GC-MS or LC-MS/MS, identifies the drug itself. It confirms positive screens and finds what the screen misses, and it can also be used as the first test.

scenes.title: Mutant IDH makes an oncometabolite
scenes.altText: Pathway schematic. Normal: isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH1/IDH2) converts isocitrate to α-ketoglutarate (α-KG). Mutant: heterozygous mutations at arginine residues (IDH1 R132H; IDH2 R140Q, R172K) give a new (neomorphic) activity that reduces α-KG to D-2-hydroxyglutarate (D-2-HG), consuming NADPH; production rises more than 100-fold. D-2-HG resembles α-KG and competitively inhibits α-KG-dependent dioxygenases (TET DNA demethylases, JmjC histone demethylases), altering DNA and histone methylation. Where: glioma (IDH mutations are WHO classification biomarkers in adult glioma), and also acute myeloid leukaemia (~20%), cartilaginous tumours, cholangiocarcinoma. Measured by mass spectrometry, enzymatic assays, or MR spectroscopy; for MS, CSF is suggested over serum in glioma because levels are higher.

cues.text: Normally, isocitrate dehydrogenase, IDH1 or IDH2, turns isocitrate into alpha-ketoglutarate.

Mutations at an arginine in the active site, such as IDH1 R132H, give the enzyme a new job: it reduces alpha-ketoglutarate to D-2-hydroxyglutarate, using NADPH. 2-HG output rises more than a hundredfold.
2-HG looks like alpha-ketoglutarate, so it blocks enzymes that need it, including DNA and histone demethylases. That is why it is called an oncometabolite.

IDH mutations are common in glioma, but also occur in acute myeloid leukaemia, cartilage tumours and cholangiocarcinoma. 2-HG can be measured by mass spectrometry, enzymatic assays, or MR spectroscopy.

scenes.title: Ambient mass spectrometry in the operating room
scenes.altText: Four device cards. DESI-MS (desorption electrospray ionisation, an ambient method with no complex sample preparation): detected 2-HG in glioma tissue sections within minutes during surgery; in 35 specimens, 2-HG was found in every IDH1-mutant tumour and in none with wild-type IDH1. MasSpec Pen: handheld pen delivers one water droplet to the tissue for about 3 seconds, then carries it to the mass spectrometer; no detectable tissue damage; 96.3% accuracy across 253 patient samples of four cancers (ex vivo); in 25 breast operations, 95.9% agreement with pathology; labelled as a research device. iKnife (REIMS): aspirates the smoke made by electrosurgical cutting into the mass spectrometer; result in about 1–2 seconds; tissue is destroyed by diathermy. Mini 12: a 25 kg miniature mass spectrometer using disposable paper-spray cartridges and a discontinuous atmospheric pressure interface (DAPI) that opens briefly for each scan, keeping vacuum below 10⁻⁵ Torr when closed; aimed at point-of-care use; a prototype. Hook answers: (1) confirm by GC-MS or LC-MS/MS; (2) 2-HG by mass spectrometry; (3) research ambient MS devices such as the MasSpec Pen or iKnife.

cues.text: Ambient mass spectrometry analyses samples directly, with no complex preparation. With desorption electrospray, DESI, 2-HG was detected in glioma tissue within minutes during surgery: in every IDH1-mutant tumour tested, and in none without the mutation.

The MasSpec Pen touches tissue with a single water droplet for about three seconds, without detectable damage. In twenty-five breast operations, it agreed with final pathology about ninety-six percent of the time.

The iKnife takes a different route: it sucks the smoke from electrosurgical cutting into the mass spectrometer and reports within one to two seconds, but it destroys the tissue it samples. Mini 12 is a miniature instrument whose inlet opens only briefly for each scan, protecting its vacuum.
Back to the hook. The opiate screen needs GC-MS or LC-MS/MS confirmation. 2-HG can flag an IDH-mutant glioma. Margin answers in the operating room come from research devices, not yet routine tests.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “A positive drug immunoassay is a final result” (✓ it is presumptive; cross-reactivity causes false positives; confirm with GC-MS or LC-MS/MS); “A negative screen rules the drug out” (✓ immunoassays miss some drugs, such as oxycodone on many opiate screens; mass spectrometry can find them); “2-HG is made by normal IDH” (✓ wild-type IDH makes α-KG; only mutant IDH reduces α-KG to 2-HG, in glioma and other IDH-mutant cancers).

cues.text: Trap one: a positive immunoassay screen is a final result. No: it is presumptive. Cross-reactivity causes false positives, so confirm with GC-MS or LC-MS/MS.
Trap two: a negative screen rules the drug out. No: immunoassays miss some drugs, such as oxycodone on many opiate screens.
Trap three: normal IDH makes 2-HG. No: normal IDH makes alpha-ketoglutarate. Only the mutant enzyme turns it into 2-HG.

props.title: ✗ “Positive screen = final result.”
lines: ✓ Presumptive; confirm by GC-MS or LC-MS/MS

scenes.title: Bouncer and ID scanner
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “The immunoassay is the BOUNCER who judges by family resemblance: look-alikes get stopped (false positives) and some family members slip past (false negatives). Mass spectrometry is the ID SCANNER that reads who the molecule actually is. Mutant IDH is a FORGER: it turns α-KG into 2-HG.” Tokens: bouncer = screen · scanner = confirm · forger = mutant IDH. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: the immunoassay is a bouncer who judges by family resemblance. Look-alikes get stopped, and some family members slip past. Mass spectrometry is the ID scanner that reads who the molecule really is. And mutant IDH is a forger, turning alpha-ketoglutarate into 2-HG.
Where it breaks: mass spectrometry is not automatically right, since it needs validated methods; it can be the first test, not only the second; and how much a screen cross-reacts depends on the kit.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Immunoassay screen = presumptive (false + and false −) → GC-MS or LC-MS/MS confirms”, “Mutant IDH: α-KG → 2-HG · ambient MS brings tissue answers to surgery (research devices)”.

cues.text: A drug immunoassay is only presumptive until mass spectrometry identifies the drug, mutant IDH turns alpha-ketoglutarate into the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate, and ambient mass spectrometry research devices bring tissue answers into the operating room within seconds to minutes.

props.label: Screen = presumptive (false + and −) → GC-MS / LC-MS/MS confirms
Mutant IDH: α-KG → 2-HG · ambient MS in surgery (research)

explanation.what: Plain language: a drug screen uses antibodies that react to look-alike molecules, so it can be wrong in both directions; mass spectrometry identifies the actual molecule, so it confirms. A mutated IDH enzyme makes a molecule, 2-HG, that normal cells hardly contain, so finding it flags an IDH-mutant tumour. New handheld and miniature mass spectrometers try to give these answers right beside the patient. Scientific terms: presumptive vs definitive testing, cross-reactivity, GC-MS, LC-MS/MS, isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH1/IDH2), α-ketoglutarate, D-2-hydroxyglutarate (oncometabolite), α-KG-dependent dioxygenases, ambient ionisation, desorption electrospray ionisation (DESI), rapid evaporative ionisation mass spectrometry (REIMS, iKnife), MasSpec Pen, paper spray, discontinuous atmospheric pressure interface (DAPI).
explanation.why: Antibodies recognise shape, so structurally similar drugs, metabolites or other compounds cross-react, and some drugs in a class are poorly recognised. Mass spectrometry identifies molecules specifically. Mutant IDH gains a new reaction that reduces α-KG to D-2-HG, which accumulates and inhibits α-KG-dependent enzymes, so 2-HG is a direct chemical readout of the mutation.
explanation.measure: Immunoassay: presumptive, fast, cheap, point of care; false positives from cross-reactivity (labetalol metabolite on amphetamines; quinolones on some opiates) and false negatives (oxycodone on many opiate screens). Definitive: GC-MS, LC-MS, LC-MS/MS, for confirmation or as the first test. 2-HG: measured by MS, enzymatic assay or MR spectroscopy; CSF suggested over serum for MS in glioma. DESI detected 2-HG within minutes; MasSpec Pen ~3 s droplet contact; iKnife ~1–2 s; Mini 12 vacuum below 10⁻⁵ Torr with DAPI closed.
explanation.differs: Presumptive screen vs definitive confirmation; wild-type IDH (α-KG) vs mutant IDH (2-HG); MasSpec Pen (water droplet, nondestructive) vs iKnife (electrosurgical smoke, destructive) vs DESI (tissue sections) vs Mini 12 (miniature point-of-care instrument).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: choose the confirmatory step after a positive drug screen, recognise that a negative screen can miss a drug, name 2-HG as the IDH-mutation metabolite, or match an ambient MS device with how it samples tissue.

mnemonic.text: The immunoassay is the BOUNCER who judges by family resemblance: look-alikes get stopped and some family members slip past. Mass spectrometry is the ID SCANNER that reads who the molecule really is. Mutant IDH is a FORGER that turns α-KG into 2-HG.
mnemonic.explanation: Links cross-reactivity to both false positives and false negatives, and MS to specific identification.
mnemonic.limitation: Mass spectrometry also needs validated methods and can be used as the first test, not only as the second; cross-reactivity differs by manufacturer and kit.

questions.stem: A urine opiate immunoassay is positive in a patient taking levofloxacin who denies opioid use. What is the best next step?

options.text: Confirm with a mass spectrometry method such as GC-MS or LC-MS/MS
options.rationale: Correct. The screen is presumptive; quinolones can cross-react with some opiate immunoassays, and mass spectrometry identifies the drug specifically.

options.text: Report the result as opiate positive
options.rationale: Incorrect. A screening immunoassay is presumptive, and cross-reactivity can cause false positives.

options.text: Report the result as negative because levofloxacin explains it
options.rationale: Incorrect. Cross-reactivity is a possible cause, not proof; only confirmatory testing shows whether an opiate is present.

options.text: Repeat the same immunoassay on the same specimen
options.rationale: Incorrect. The same antibody would react the same way with the same cross-reacting compound.

questions.stem: Which metabolite accumulates in tumours with mutant IDH1 or IDH2?

options.rationale: Correct. Mutant IDH reduces α-ketoglutarate to D-2-HG using NADPH.
Incorrect. α-KG is the normal product of wild-type IDH; the mutant enzyme consumes it.
Incorrect. Isocitrate is the substrate of the normal IDH reaction.
Incorrect. Phenylalanine is not the product of the IDH reaction; mutant IDH makes 2-HG.

questions.stem: Which ambient mass spectrometry approach analyses the smoke produced by electrosurgical cutting?

options.text: iKnife (rapid evaporative ionisation mass spectrometry, REIMS)
options.rationale: Correct. The iKnife aspirates the aerosol from electrosurgical dissection into the mass spectrometer and reports within seconds.
Incorrect. The MasSpec Pen extracts molecules with a water droplet and causes no detectable tissue damage.
Incorrect. In the glioma study, DESI analysed tissue sections, for example to detect 2-HG.
Incorrect. Mini 12 is a miniature mass spectrometer that uses paper-spray cartridges, for example for drugs in blood.

claims.text: Immunoassay screens are presumptive; cross-reactivity causes false positives (labetalol, quinolones) and some drugs are missed (oxycodone); cross-reactivity varies by kit; GC-MS and LC-MS/MS identify drugs specifically and confirm or act as initial tests.

Mutant IDH1/IDH2 reduces α-KG to D-2-HG using NADPH; D-2-HG inhibits α-KG-dependent dioxygenases; IDH-mutant cancers include glioma, AML, cartilaginous tumours, cholangiocarcinoma; 2-HG measured by MS, enzymatic assay or MRS.
DESI-MS detected 2-HG intraoperatively within minutes, in all IDH1-mutant and no wild-type gliomas studied.

MasSpec Pen droplet sampling, nondestructive, accuracy figures and research-device status; iKnife smoke analysis in about 1–2 s, destructive; Mini 12 paper spray, DAPI and vacuum, point-of-care prototype.
USS Nimitz 1981 history; GC-MS as the traditional confirmatory standard; iKnife 1.8-second and 94.4% figures; MasSpec Pen mouse figures; Mini 12 resolution, mass range and MSn specifications.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 5 Hit 1 and Trap 6 say immunoassays “err toward false positives”. Argoff 2018 and Reschly-Krasowski 2018 also report false negatives (for example oxycodone poorly detected by many opiate screens), and definitive MS testing can be used as the initial test, not only to confirm (register flag rv-ch5-immunoassay-false-negatives).

Ch. 5 Hit 10 presents 2-HG as the IDH-mutation marker in glioma. Chou 2021 lists IDH1/2 mutations, and so 2-HG accumulation, also in AML (~20%), cartilaginous tumours and cholangiocarcinoma (register flag rv-ch5-2hg-beyond-glioma).

Ch. 5 Hit 11 says ambient MS “goes to the bedside”. Garza 2024 labels the MasSpec Pen a research device only, and Li 2014 calls Mini 12 a proof-of-concept prototype; open sources give iKnife response as about 1–2 s (0.7–2.5 s) rather than a single 1.8-s figure (register flag rv-ch5-ambient-ms-research-stage).
